brief: Citadel Securities' Shah argues Nvidia executes fine near-term without Jensen Huang (Q3 revenue beat, raised 2028 growth outlook) but long-term risk appetite for unproven bets erodes without a founder willing to make them, and new management is already acting more conservative: a Q4 outlook assuming zero China compute revenue and a CFO citing customers' access to capital. Separately, Shah distinguishes AI demand, model-development profitability, and returns on owning compute: physical data-center scarcity is intact (supply up 33.7% YoY, vacancy near record lows), so compute already in service keeps a premium, but regulation aimed at model development rather than construction would weaken the demand that premium depends on. Anthropic's S-1 shows revenue growing fast but compute costs growing faster, with ~$900bn of commitments against ~$132bn cash, reducing Shah's three hurdles (inference margin, research cost, return on capital) to things strong demand helps but does not guarantee, leading him to prefer diversified platforms over single frontier labs. Hot GDP, payrolls, wages and CPI data raise December 50bp hike odds per Waller; only productivity offers relief. A controlled AI capex slowdown is manageable, Shah says, but an outright stop would hit growth, earnings and rates simultaneously.
